clue.text: Don't remove clothes from the washing line, but from oneself, perhaps?

definitions.text: Don't remove clothes from the washing line, but from oneself, perhaps?

parts.words: Don't remove clothes from the washing line, but from oneself, perhaps?
parts.note: read literally, the phrase says leave all the washing dangling on the line; applied to oneself it means behave with no inhibitions at all

explanation.surface: Laundry advice that suddenly turns into an invitation to strip off.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to behave in a completely relaxed, uninhibited way, the cryptic reading picturing everything left dangling.

clue.text: Daniel and James are favoured

parts.note: Daniel and James are both books of the Bible, the Good Book, so they sit in the Good Book's books; the idiom for being favoured follows

explanation.surface: Two men, Daniel and James, enjoy someone's approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in someone's good books is an idiom for enjoying their favour; Daniel and James are literally among the Bible's books.

clue.text: Bligh, perhaps, buries each hat in soil

indicators.note: the soil word covers over the other pieces, holding them inside it

parts.note: to soil is to stain
a cap is a hat

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps Bligh, buries a hat in the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link word, since 'buries' already gives the container. William Bligh was captain of HMS Bounty, famous for its mutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: William Bligh, captain of HMS Bounty, is an example of a ship's master, signalled by 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Defendant finally having to stand before court, split twice

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word Defendant

parts.note: to stand up is to rise

explanation.surface: A defendant must eventually stand up before the court.
explanation.definitionFit: To trisect is to divide into three parts, which takes two cuts, so splitting twice.

clue.text: Short-change with word of approval

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to amend is to change

explanation.surface: Being short-changed while someone says a word of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short-change' looks like one familiar word, but 'Short' trims the last letter from AMEND, a synonym of 'change'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said after a prayer to express agreement or assent, so it is a word of approval.

clue.text: Appear gauche, sans droite?

parts.note: gauche is French for left and also English for clumsy; sans droite means without a right, so both feet are left ones

explanation.surface: A French-flavoured remark about looking awkward with no right side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone said to have two left feet is clumsy, especially at dancing, which is being gauche; French 'gauche' also means left.

clue.text: Where those inside out?

parts.note: in cricket the batsmen who have been dismissed are out, and they sit inside the clubhouse by the field

explanation.surface: A riddle asking where the people indoors are actually out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to talk about clothes turned inside out. In cricket, a batter who has been dismissed is 'out' and goes back into the pavilion, the clubhouse beside the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The pavilion is the building at a cricket ground where dismissed batsmen, now out, sit inside.

clue.text: Beast gets on home beside two rivers

parts.note: RE means on, as in regarding, in crossword usage
at home is in
the Dee is a river in Britain, and R abbreviates river; together they are the two rivers
the Dee is a river in Britain, and R abbreviates river; together they are the two rivers

explanation.surface: An animal gets settled at a house standing between two rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A reindeer is a large deer of the Arctic, an example of a beast or animal.

clue.text: Given some time, a greyhound appears thin

indicators.note: some of the words is used, so the answer sits inside the run time, a greyhound

explanation.surface: Given time, a greyhound grows lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means lacking in quantity or substance, a synonym for thin or scanty.

clue.text: Writer's people accepting what's charged has mechanical parts

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for an adjective describing something with mechanical parts

indicators.note: the pen-makers' name takes in the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: Bic is the firm that makes a familiar ballpoint, a writer, so its people are Bic
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: An author's staff take in someone charged with a crime who has prosthetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests a criminal charge but means electrical charge. Bic is a ballpoint pen brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Bionic describes a body enhanced with electronic or mechanical parts, as in science-fiction cyborgs.

clue.text: A basic of written exam? Pass it!

definitions.meaning: a grammatical unit of written language is one of the basic building blocks of any written paper
a judge passes judgement on a convicted person, a punishment that is passed

explanation.definitionFit: A sentence is a basic grammatical unit of writing, and judges pass a sentence on the guilty.

clue.text: Fish given deepest line?

definitions.meaning: a sea or freshwater fish of the perch family
in music the lowest part in a harmony is the line sung or played deepest

explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a fish, and the bass line is the lowest-pitched part in music.

clue.text: Fantastic black bird goes in for each quickie

indicators.note: the pieces go into the word for 'for each', which wraps round them

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per head'
ace means excellent, fantastic
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: An amazing dark bird enters for each quick event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' looks like an anagram signal but means ACE. In cricket a quickie is a fast bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A quickie is slang for a fast bowler in cricket, one who relies on speed through the air.

clue.text: Red Army unfortunately in the drink

parts.note: blood-red, so bloody

indicators.note: things gone unfortunately are messed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sadly, the Red Army ends up in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the drink' suggests falling into the sea; 'unfortunately' rearranges ARMY to MARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bloody Mary is a cocktail of vodka and tomato juice, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Music maker providing a casual environment for reclining drunkard

indicators.note: the casual word forms the surroundings for the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: lax means relaxed, casual

indicators.note: lying back, so the drunkard word is laid down backwards

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: An easygoing setting for a drunk lying back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reclining' turns the drunkard backwards, giving TOS; 'environment for' puts it inside the casual word.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto sax is a saxophone pitched in the alto range, an instrument, so a music maker.

clue.text: Lumps requiring surgery in inanimate figures

indicators.note: the surgery piece is placed in the figures word

parts.note: dolls are lifeless human figures
OP is short for an operation, surgery

explanation.surface: Growths needing an operation are found in toy figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Dollops are shapeless lumps or blobs of soft food, so dollops and lumps are synonyms.

clue.text: Harden when state beginning to freeze — outside icy winds

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit outside the single letter, enclosing it
winds as in twists, so the letters of icy are turned around into a new order
the beginning of the word freeze, its first letter

explanation.surface: Something hardens as the land starts to freeze under icy winds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' looks like weather but rearranges ICY into CIY, which goes outside F.
explanation.definitionFit: To calcify is to harden by deposits of calcium salts, so it means to harden or stiffen.

clue.text: Employee already prepared to be roman-tically attached

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand
a thing in hand is already under way or prepared

explanation.surface: A worker who is all set gets involved in a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'roman-tically' splits off the Roman: lovers walking hand in hand, as in the Latin manus.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples walk hand in hand when romantically attached, holding each other's hands.

clue.text: Figure, itself seen in expression of disgust

indicators.note: the figure itself is seen in the expression, placed within it

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust
the figure itself as a Roman numeral, V

explanation.surface: A number appears within a cry of disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'itself' means the figure in question written as a Roman numeral, V.
explanation.definitionFit: Five is a number, and a number written down is a figure.

clue.text: One doubts coasting is all at sea

indicators.note: someone all at sea is confused, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that coasting means drifting at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic doubts or does not know whether God exists, so is one who doubts.

clue.text: Driver's signal going either way

indicators.note: the letters read the same in either direction, forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A motorist's horn blast can go either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A toot is a short blast on a car horn, a driver's signal.

clue.text: Cross about anything but silent silence

indicators.note: the cross wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed about a total lack of silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry' but is the hybrid MULE. FF is the musical mark for very loud.
explanation.definitionFit: To muffle is to deaden or suppress sound, so it is a verb meaning to silence.

clue.text: One flying round the bend

explanation.definitionFit: A cuckoo is a bird, and as slang the word means crazy or mad.

clue.text: Hair under ruffle

parts.note: fur is animal hair
below means under

explanation.surface: Hair beneath a frilly collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A furbelow is a flounce or gathered frill on a dress, a ruffle.
